comparisons.reason: Both use OC_comments with any-comment binary and the same null/empty rules, but the constructs differ in scope. Left requires a specific, verifiable procedural example, meaning a concrete description of an actual procedure, process, rule or protocol, such as how a legal or institutional process works. Right accepts any specific real-world example of any type (event, person, organization, place, study, statistic, historical instance). Right is materially broader, so a comment citing a statistic or a person would score 1 on right and 0 on left. Left also says to ignore quoted OP text, and right has no such rule.
